name: Zelio E Mobility Ltd
title: Zelio E Mobility Ltd - 544563 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: H1 FY27 revenue Rs 296.66 cr (more than double YoY) and PAT Rs 31.39 cr, but operating cash flow negative, borrowings up to Rs 44.82 cr, and guidance was reiterated with no numbers changed; utilisation of new plants is low at 30-50%.

triggers.label: Utilisation ~40-50%, new plants 30-50%
triggers.quote: Right now our utilization is almost 40-50%.

triggers.label: Operating cash flow negative; borrowings Rs 44.82 cr
triggers.quote: our operating cash flow for the half was negative and our borrings went up to Rs. 44.82 crore.

triggers.label: FY27 guidance reiterated, not raised
triggers.quote: more than 125,000 units more than 550 dealers new high speed models and revenue growth of 75 to 80%

triggers.label: Import duty dispute; peers in same boat
triggers.quote: we are fighting for it. We have appealed in our customs.

summary.headline: Zelio E Mobility H1 FY27 revenue rose to Rs 296.66 crore (more than double YoY), with PAT of Rs 31.39 crore and net margin above 10%.
summary.overview: Management described H1 FY27 (six months to 30 September 2026) as the strongest half in the company's history, with consolidated revenue from operations of Rs 296.66 crore, more than double the prior-year period, and EBITDA of Rs 40.49 crore at a 13.6% margin (12% a year earlier). Profit after tax was Rs 31.39 crore, with EPS of Rs 14.24. Growth was funded partly by working capital: inventory and supplier advances pushed operating cash flow negative and borrowings up to Rs 44.82 crore, with debt-to-equity at 0.31x versus 0.18x in March. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of more than 125,000 units, 550+ dealers, and 75-80% revenue growth, and a fourth plant in Patan began commercial production on 28 October.

financial_highlights.change: margin up from 12% in H1 FY26
equal to about 98% of FY26 full-year EPS

segments.name: Two-wheeler (low speed scooters)
segments.commentary: Sold more than 62,000 units in H1 FY27 versus more than 70,000 in all of FY26. Low-speed is the bulk of sales; high-speed share is small, with 2-3 high-speed models planned next year.

segments.name: Three-wheeler (e-rickshaw / cargo, Tanga)
segments.commentary: Sold about 600 units in H1 FY27 versus about 650 in full FY26. Management targets 2,000-3,000 units from next financial year, with Patan plant intended to bring sourcing in-house.

segments.name: Export / Nepal
segments.commentary: Selling more than 160 scooters a month in Nepal; a distributor outlet opened in Kathmandu last month.

segments.name: Geographic: West Bengal
segments.commentary: Management said monthly sales in West Bengal rose to 1,400-1,500 scooters from about 600 a year earlier.

guidance_outlook: FY27: more than 125,000 units, more than 550 dealers (currently about 400-450 across 25+ states), new high-speed models, and revenue growth of 75-80%.
Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1, citing the Diwali season in November; it declined to give a H2 revenue or profit number.
Working capital expected to ease as inventory converts to sales in H2; management said it will report progress next time.
FY30 vision: more than 1 million scooters a year and at least 25% market share; no revenue target disclosed.
High-speed entry planned with 2-3 models next year; products submitted for ICAT/ARAI approval.
Management said it will never trade profit for growth.
capex_capacity: Patan (Hissar, Haryana) fourth plant started commercial production on 28 October 2026; adds 72,000 units a year (42,000 two-wheeler, 24,000 three-wheeler, plus others), investment above Rs 20 crore, largely backward integration.
Odisha plant started production in February 2026; Coimbatore followed in July 2026.
Installed capacity is 3.12 lakh units across four plants (Haryana, Odisha, Coimbatore, Patan).
Utilisation: Patan 70-80%, Odisha about 50%, Coimbatore about 30% (started three months earlier); overall utilisation cited as 40-50% in one answer.
Rs 168 crore preferential issue approved by shareholders last month, including promoter warrants; proceeds for R&D team, motor and battery pack development, and backward integration.
demand_pricing: Average SKU price cited at about Rs 45,000, rising to about Rs 48,000-50,000 due to metal price increases; management said demand held despite 10-15% raw material inflation.
Management claims 8-9% share of the low-speed market, targeting 25% within two years; competition in low-speed described as limited, with new entrants at small scale.
About 2 months of advance orders on hand for the remaining four months of the season, per management.

Import dependence: Tanga about 20-30% imported (electrical parts); two-wheeler about 30% of SKUs imported and most of the rest sourced from third parties; batteries imported from Vietnam, Malaysia and China.
Battery replacement ratio about 3-4%. Management is contesting a customs notice on imports; it said the whole industry is affected.

qa_highlights.question: How much of H1 revenue growth is from volume versus price or mix, and what is the product-wise split?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler volume was over 62,000 units in H1 against more than 70,000 in all of FY26; three-wheeler about 600 units against about 650 in FY26. ASP rose from about Rs 45,000 to Rs 48,000-50,000 on metal prices. Low-speed is the majority of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What are the utilisation levels of the four plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Patan 70-80%, Odisha about 50%, Coimbatore about 30%. Management expects 80% utilisation of the Patan plant within two years.

qa_highlights.question: How is competition from new entrants and well-funded players affecting the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market is growing about 50% a year and that the company competes on quality and service; it claims 8-9% low-speed share and targets 25% within two years.

qa_highlights.question: How will commodity inflation affect demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand has not been affected by 10-15% raw material increases, as rising fuel prices have increased demand; prices have been raised across the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter high-speed, and what R&D is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: High-speed entry is planned with 2-3 models next year, targeting affordable pricing. The Rs 168 crore raise funds a professional R&D team focused on motors and battery packs, and backward integration; management said results are 2-3 years away.

qa_highlights.question: Is B2B or delivery-fleet business planned, and what is the outlook for Nepal and other markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B margins and brand visibility are low, so it is focused on B2C through dealers for now, with B2B possible later when capacity is spare. Nepal sales exceed 160 scooters a month; no other international markets are active.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow and borrowings of Rs 44.82 crore; debt-to-equity rose to 0.31x from 0.18x in March. Watch whether working capital eases in H2.
Inventory build ahead of the festive season; the company says it is for the season already under way.
Import dependence (batteries, electricals, Tanga parts) and a customs notice the company is contesting.
Competition from new entrants and larger players in low-speed and in the high-speed segment, where the company has no products yet.
Ramp-up risk at Coimbatore (30% utilisation) and Odisha (about 50%); the Patan plant's sourcing shift in-house depends on its execution.
Policy risk on low-speed vehicle regulation (motor power limits and unregistered-vehicle enforcement), per management comments.
Management did not disclose a H2 revenue or profit number; shareholders should watch for a formal H2 target.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional, with a strong focus on delivering prior commitments. Management was candid about working-capital strain but gave few hard numbers on H2, high-speed economics or R&D spend; several answers were vague or repetitive.
key_quotes: Let me say it upfront, this has been the strongest half-year in Zelio's history and the results are as good as we had planned or in many ways better.
Our debt to equity is now 0.31 times against 0.18 times in March.
We will never trade profit for any devolved.
Every rupee has gone where we told you it would.

adds.what: Patan (Hissar, Haryana) fourth plant, adds 72,000 units a year
High-speed scooter models (2-3 models planned next year), not a plant

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 75-80% revenue growth (midpoint 77.5%), more than 125,000 units and 550+ dealers was reiterated, not raised; backed by the Patan plant (72,000 units/yr, live 28 Oct), about two months of advance orders for the rest of the season, and Odisha and Coimbatore ramp-ups, but management gave no H2 revenue number and utilisation is only 40-50%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 13.6% in H1 FY27 from 12% a year earlier, but ASP rises on metal prices and 10-15% raw material inflation make the H2 margin path unclear, with no H2 profit number given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Patan fourth plant (72,000 units/yr, Rs 20+ crore) started commercial production on 28 October 2026, so new capacity is already live; installed capacity is 3.12 lakh units.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guidance of more than 125,000 units for FY27 implies H2 volume well above H1's 62,000+ two-wheeler units, backed by about 2 months of advance orders and the Diwali season.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Blended utilisation is only 40-50% (Patan 70-80%, Odisha about 50%, Coimbatore about 30%), so a new plant is unlikely near term, though the Rs 168 crore raise and R&D/backward integration spend could bring further capex announcements.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of 75-80% revenue growth, more than 125,000 units and 550+ dealers was only reiterated, not raised, and no H2 revenue or profit number was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Operating cash flow is negative, borrowings rose to Rs 44.82 crore (D/E 0.31x from 0.18x), and current dealers are 400-450 against a 550 target, so the volume and dealer targets carry execution risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans 2-3 high-speed scooter models next year and has submitted products for ICAT/ARAI approval; no high-speed product exists yet.

rows.label: Working capital easing in H2
rows.why: Inventory and supplier advances pushed operating cash flow negative; management says inventory converts to sales in H2 but gave no figure, and receivables are under 6 days.

rows.label: Dealer network to 550+
rows.why: Dealers are about 400-450 across 25+ states today against a 550+ target, and management reaffirmed it, so a 25%+ dealer expansion is needed in the remaining months.

rows.label: Nepal and West Bengal demand
rows.why: Nepal sells more than 160 scooters a month with a Kathmandu outlet just opened, and West Bengal monthly sales rose to 1,400-1,500 from about 600 a year earlier.

tone.note: Management was confident about the Patan plant, the Diwali-driven H2 and FY27 guidance, but cautious on working capital, import exposure and high-speed economics; analysts pressed on the H2 numbers, utilisation and cash flow, and answers were often vague.
